newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals end mixed after quiet session.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals end mixed after quiet session.

text.p: New York precious metals futures ended mixed in a quiet, lightly traded post-Christmas Day holiday session with many still away from their desks.
The London bullion market was also closed Thursday due to Boxing Day, a U.K. public holiday. The market reopens Friday.
Gains in silver were due to light fund buying, but no fresh news lay behind platinum's losses, traders said.
COMEX February gold went out 50 cents higher at $371.10 cents an ounce, traded $371.40 to $370.80. New York bullion was quoted at $369.00/$369.50 mid-afternoon.
COMEX March silver ended 5.5 cents up at $4.928 an ounce.
Estimated volume in gold and silver were just 3,000 and 5,000 lots, respectively.
Although gold and silver remained firmer throughout the session, the white metals were mixed, with platinum posting losses from the opening bell.
Thin volume helped to exaggerate moves, traders said.
NYMEX April platinum ended $1.20 lower at $375.10 an ounce, off the day's low of $374.50. January platinum ended $1.40 down at $373.00.
NYMEX March palladium was barely changed for much of the session but was able to nudge higher in late trading, closing up 60 cents at $119.40 cents. Volume was very light at an estimated 66 lots.
